stories.headline: Gong Launches 'Mission Big Dipper' — Adds Agentic Execution Layer to Revenue AI Operating System
stories.summary: In late June 2026, Gong announced Mission Big Dipper, introducing a new agentic execution layer across its Revenue AI Operating System — going well beyond call recording into autonomous revenue workflow orchestration. This follows ARR surpassing $500M on 55%+ year-over-year growth, driven by enterprise consolidation onto AI-native revenue platforms. For D&B, this signals the speed at which revenue AI vendors are building agent infrastructure: Gong's Revenue Graph is a proprietary data moat that mirrors D&B's own logic — whoever owns the authoritative data layer wins the agent stack. D&B's Buydex and DUNS signals could be the 'ground truth' feed that makes Gong's agents decisively smarter on company identity and financial risk.

stories.headline: Deloitte State of AI 2026: Only 1-in-5 Enterprises Has Mature Governance for Agentic AI
stories.summary: Deloitte's 2026 State of AI in the Enterprise report finds that while 23% of companies now report at least moderate agentic AI use, only one in five has a mature governance model for autonomous agents. The governance gap is most acute where agents touch financial processes and customer interactions — exactly the domains where D&B's explainability-first positioning has structural value. This is a direct market signal: enterprises deploying agentic AI for sales, credit, and procurement decisions need auditable, verified data foundations — a gap D&B's DUNS entity resolution and Paydex scores are built to fill.

stories.headline: Walnut Launches AI Agent Platform for B2B Buyer Experience — Targets Go-to-Market Teams
stories.summary: Walnut, used by hundreds of B2B software go-to-market teams, launched a family of AI agents in early September 2026 designed to personalise the buying experience at scale — including an in-product agent that lets buyers navigate demos via natural language. The move reflects accelerating commoditisation of the buyer-facing AI layer in B2B sales, with personalisation shifting from rep-driven to agent-driven. For D&B, this reinforces the Prospecting and Account Intelligence agent archetypes: as buyer-side agents proliferate, the quality of firmographic and intent data embedded in those agents becomes the differentiator — a role D&B's data cloud is positioned to play.

stories.headline: Informa TechTarget Launches B2B AI Authority Index to Track Brand Visibility in AI Search
stories.summary: Informa TechTarget this week launched the B2B AI Authority Index, a tool that uses AI analytical models to measure how business software buyers discover and cite brands within AI search engines like Perplexity and ChatGPT. As AI-mediated discovery replaces traditional SEO and demand gen, this is a direct threat to legacy lead-generation models — including intent data products that rely on web-based behavioural tracking. For D&B, it underscores the urgency of embedding D&B signals natively into AI agent workflows: if AI agents are increasingly the first point of brand evaluation for B2B buyers, D&B data must be present at that layer, not downstream.

stories.headline: Procurement Software Is Evolving Fast — AI Agents Are Rewriting the Purchase Order Playbook
stories.summary: B2B News Network's September 9 analysis reports that procurement software is undergoing a fundamental shift, moving well beyond purchase order routing as AI agents begin managing supplier evaluation, approval workflows, and spend decisions autonomously. This is directly relevant to D&B's Pipeline Risk & Revenue Protection and Territory & Market Planning agent archetypes: autonomous procurement agents making supplier or vendor decisions will need real-time financial risk scores, entity resolution, and corporate family tree data to operate safely. D&B's Paydex, Supplier Evaluation Risk Rating, and DUNS hierarchy are the exact inputs these agents require — making embedded D&B data a procurement risk standard, not just a sales tool.

stories.headline: PwC Projects $31.6 Trillion in Global AI Infrastructure Investment Through 2050 — Power Flagged as Decisive Constraint
stories.summary: PwC's Global Data Centre Outlook, published September 2, calculates that $31.6 trillion in cumulative capex will be needed through 2050 to build AI compute capacity, with annual data centre spend forecast to more than double from roughly $800 billion in 2026 to $1.8 trillion by 2050. Crucially, PwC identifies recurring chip upgrades — not construction — as the dominant long-term cost driver, and flags power access as the single factor most likely to determine where investment flows. For D&B, this underscores why the 'persistent data layer' framing matters: as infrastructure economics get more extreme, the premium on data assets that make every inference count — entity resolution, Paydex, Buydex — only rises.

stories.headline: Labs Race to Gate Dangerous Cyber Capabilities — Tiered Access Becomes September's Defining Model Architecture Move
stories.summary: Four frontier model launches in 72 hours at the start of September — Claude Fable 5.1, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Meta's Muse Spark 1.3, and OpenAI Astra — shared a common architectural theme: shipping a general-release model alongside a separately gated, security-focused capability tier with tighter access controls. Anthropic's Mythos 5.1, Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, and OpenAI's Astra all implement this split, with labs citing benchmark evidence that offensive cyber reasoning now emerges from ordinary post-training scaling. This is a direct policy-architecture response, not a product differentiator — and signals that self-governance on dangerous capabilities is being operationalised at the model level before regulators mandate it.

stories.headline: NVIDIA Mobilises Australian Data Centre Ecosystem for Up to 2-Gigawatt AI Buildout by 2027
stories.summary: Announced September 10, NVIDIA is partnering with a group of Australian cloud and data centre operators — including IREN, NEXTDC, AirTrunk, and others — to expand land, power, and shell capacity designed to host multiple generations of NVIDIA AI infrastructure, targeting up to 2 gigawatts by 2027. NVIDIA will deliver its DSX platform, accelerated computing, and networking while partners operate the AI factories. The move is a clear sovereignty play, extending NVIDIA's 'AI factory' model beyond the US and Europe and into the Asia-Pacific region — directly relevant to D&B's own geographic data coverage and the opportunity to position DUNS-anchored entity resolution as the neutral data layer across sovereign AI deployments.

stories.headline: Texas TRAIGA Complaint Mechanism Goes Live in September — State AI Enforcement Era Formally Begins
stories.summary: Texas's AI law TRAIGA (HB 149) activates its attorney general complaint mechanism this month, marking one of the first state-level AI enforcement tools to go operational in the US. This sits alongside a growing patchwork: nearly 100 chatbot-specific bills introduced across 34 states, Illinois's SB 315 AI Safety Measures Act signed in July, and Colorado's replacement of its AI Act under SB 26-189. The US regulatory picture is now genuinely multi-layered — federal preemption pressure from Trump's December 2025 executive order pulling in one direction, aggressive state enforcement in the other. For D&B, explainability and auditable data provenance are no longer just sales differentiators; they are compliance infrastructure that enterprise buyers increasingly need to demonstrate to regulators.

stories.headline: UK Government Moves to Restrict Trade in Goods from Israeli Settlements
stories.summary: Foreign Secretary David Lammy made a statement in the House of Commons this week announcing measures restricting trade in goods originating from Israeli settlements, a significant escalation in UK policy. The Chair of the International Development Committee welcomed the announcement, describing it as a meaningful step. The move is likely to generate substantial political debate in Westminster and test UK-US relations given the current Washington administration's stance on Israel.

stories.headline: Republican National Convention Opens in Dallas as Trump Signals Second-Term Agenda
stories.summary: President Trump addressed delegates on the first day of the 2026 Republican National Convention at the American Airlines Center in Dallas on 9 September, setting the tone for the November midterm campaign. The convention comes as Democrats and Republicans have found rare common ground on certain issues this election cycle, according to NPR. Separately, Common Cause filed a sweeping federal lawsuit on 10 September alleging that agencies are illegally surveilling those who observe immigration enforcement activity.

stories.headline: Physicists Directly Observe Quantum Effect of Gravity in Landmark Einstein Test
stories.summary: Scientists reported on 8 September that they have directly observed a long-predicted quantum effect of gravity using ultracold atoms, delivering one of the most striking experimental tests of Einstein's foundational ideas to date. The result had been theoretically anticipated for decades but had resisted experimental confirmation until now. Separately, a new analysis of over 1,700 supernovae is also questioning whether the universe is truly accelerating in its expansion — a challenge to one of cosmology's core assumptions.

stories.headline: Amgen Irish Open Enters Weekend Rounds at Trump's Doonbeg — BMW PGA Next
stories.summary: The Amgen Irish Open at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg is currently mid-tournament (running 10–13 September) with no final result yet confirmed as of Friday morning. The field is competing for DP World Tour Race to Dubai points ahead of the season's flagship Rolex Series event, the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth, which follows next week (17–20 September). The PGA Tour's next scheduled event is the Biltmore Championship Asheville on 17 September, meaning there is no concurrent PGA Tour event this week.

stories.headline: England's Post-World Cup 2026 Qualifying Campaign Gets Under Way — First Fixtures Confirmed
stories.summary: With the 2026 World Cup concluded in July — where England reached the semi-finals before losing 2-1 to Argentina and then beat France to finish third — Thomas Tuchel's side now turns its attention to the next qualification cycle. The first European qualifying fixtures in England's new group begin on 26 September against Spain, with further matches against Czechia and Croatia to follow. The Premier League international break this week has given Tuchel his first formal squad session since the tournament.

stories.headline: Gallagher Premiership 2026-27 Season Confirmed as Franchise Model Era Begins on 25 September
stories.summary: The new Gallagher Premiership season kicks off on 25 September, marking a historic structural shift: it will be the first campaign contested under a franchise-based model following the RFU council's approval in February 2026 to abolish automatic promotion and relegation. Reigning champions Northampton Saints, who claimed their third title in 2025-26, enter as the team to beat. The competition will be broadcast by TNT Sports for a fourteenth consecutive year, with select matches free-to-air on ITV.

stories.headline: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Launches to Probe the Hidden Universe
stories.summary: NASA's long-awaited Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope successfully launched on 30 August on a mission described as probing the 'hidden universe', targeting dark energy, dark matter and exoplanet populations at unprecedented scale. NASA is inviting the public to 'claim a pixel' on the telescope's first images, which will represent a patch of the cosmos never seen at this resolution before. The launch follows an earlier delay to the Crew-13 Dragon mission after an oxidiser leak was found during pre-launch preparations on 1 September.

stories.headline: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face: What It Means When the Chip Maker Owns the Model Marketplace
stories.summary: Ben Thompson's September 4 Dithering episode examines Nvidia's reported acquisition of Hugging Face, arguing it represents a dramatic vertical integration play — Nvidia moving from selling compute to controlling the open-weights distribution layer. If the chip maker owns the marketplace where models live, it gains leverage over both the supply (model creators) and demand (enterprise deployers) sides of the AI stack simultaneously. For D&B, this is a direct signal that neutrality is under pressure: the 'be everywhere' strategy requires the distribution layer to remain open, and a Nvidia-owned Hugging Face could start tilting the playing field. It reinforces why D&B's value must be anchored in proprietary data (DUNS, Paydex, Buydex) rather than any single platform relationship.

stories.headline: 2026 State of AI Agents: Multi-Agent Systems Grew 327% — But Governance Is the Blocker
stories.summary: Databricks' widely circulated enterprise report shows that organisations worldwide are rapidly shifting from single chatbots to multi-agent systems, which grew by 327% in under four months, yet companies using evaluation and governance tools get nearly 6–12x more AI projects into production. The report makes clear that raw deployment volume is no longer the differentiator — structured data foundations, governed tool access, and evaluation frameworks are what separate pilots from production. This is a direct validation of D&B's 'Explainability First / Ground Truth' thesis: agents that can't verify the entities and companies they act on are governance liabilities, not assets. D&B's entity resolution and corporate family trees are exactly the kind of verifiable data substrate the governance gap demands.
stories.source: Databricks Research — 2026 State of AI Agents (widely circulated September 2026)

stories.headline: Trusted Agentic AI Landscape Q3 2026: Lock-In Is Moving from the Model Layer to the Stack Layer
stories.summary: Kai Waehner's August/September 2026 update to his enterprise agentic AI landscape map argues that following a US export-control episode that briefly suspended access to frontier models, enterprise risk managers are now focused less on which model to use and more on which stack layer creates irreversible dependency. The analysis positions every major vendor — Microsoft, Google, AWS, Anthropic, Salesforce, SAP — on two axes: trust and flexibility, finding that lock-in is quietly migrating from model choice up into orchestration, data pipelines, and agent infrastructure. For D&B, this is a clear strategic green light: as stack-layer lock-in tightens around orchestration platforms, a vendor-neutral data layer that embeds across all of them (Copilot, Agentforce, Bedrock, ServiceNow) becomes structurally indispensable rather than optional. The trust dimension also maps directly to D&B's explainability positioning — enterprises won't grant agents autonomous action unless the underlying data is auditable.
stories.source: Kai Waehner, kai-waehner.de — Trusted Agentic AI Landscape Q3 2026 (August/September 2026)

data_science.tagline: The shared memory layer that stops your ML teams rebuilding the same features over and over — and keeps training and serving data in sync.
data_science.what_it_is: A Feature Store is a centralised data system purpose-built for machine learning. It sits between your raw data sources and your models, and does two things: (1) it computes and stores engineered features so they can be reused across models and teams, and (2) it guarantees that the features your model trained on are byte-for-byte identical to what it sees at inference time. Without it, every data scientist hand-rolls the same transformations, training pipelines diverge from serving pipelines, and subtle timestamp leakage silently poisons your models. Think of it as a versioned, queryable catalogue of 'the facts we know about an entity at a given point in time' — exactly the kind of language D&B lives in.
data_science.how_it_works:
A Feature Store has four interlocking components:

1. **Offline Store (historical)** — A columnar store (Parquet on S3, BigQuery, Snowflake) holding point-in-time correct feature snapshots. When you train, you ask: 'Give me the features for company DUNS 123456789 *as they existed on 2025-03-01*, not as they look today.' This is called a point-in-time join and it is the single most important correctness guarantee a Feature Store provides.

2. **Online Store (low-latency)** — A key-value store (Redis, DynamoDB, Cassandra) holding the *latest* feature values for live inference. When a Prospecting Agent needs a real-time risk score on a new prospect, it reads from here in <10ms.

3. **Feature Pipeline / Transformation Layer** — Code (SQL, PySpark, dbt, Python) that defines how raw data becomes features. These definitions are versioned and reused. You write 'paydex_90d_trend' once; every model that needs it reads the same definition.

4. **Feature Registry / Metadata** — A catalogue recording what each feature means, who owns it, when it was last computed, which models consume it, and its lineage back to source data. This is your explainability and governance surface.

**The training-serving skew problem** is why all of this matters. If your training pipeline computes 'days_since_last_payment' using a Python script and your serving pipeline computes it differently in Java, your model's live accuracy will silently degrade. The Feature Store enforces a single definition executed once, consumed everywhere.

Popular implementations: **Feast** (open-source, cloud-agnostic), **Tecton** (managed, enterprise-grade), **Hopsworks** (open-source with strong streaming support), **Databricks Feature Store** (native to the Lakehouse), **AWS SageMaker Feature Store**, **Vertex AI Feature Store** (GCP).
data_science.when_to_use: Use a Feature Store when: (a) more than one model shares the same input features — duplication cost is already real; (b) you have a training-to-production gap and live accuracy is mysteriously worse than validation accuracy; (c) regulatory or audit requirements demand feature lineage (who computed this, from what, when?); (d) you are building real-time scoring pipelines where sub-100ms latency matters; (e) your ML team has grown beyond two people and feature definitions are being passed around in Slack messages. You do NOT need one if you have a single experimental model with no production deployment — the overhead is not justified at that scale.
data_science.worked_example:
**D&B use case: Real-Time Account Expansion Agent**

D&B's Account Expansion agent archetype monitors existing customer accounts for cross-sell and upsell signals. Here is how a Feature Store makes this production-grade:

**Features defined once in the registry:**
- `duns_paydex_delta_90d` — change in Paydex score over 90 days (payment behaviour trend)
- `corporate_family_headcount_growth_yoy` — year-on-year employee count change across the full D&B corporate family tree
- `buydex_category_spend_rank` — percentile rank of estimated spend in a product category vs peer companies
- `days_since_last_contract_renewal` — computed from CRM events
- `intent_signal_spike_30d` — binary flag: did Bombora/G2 intent scores spike >2 standard deviations in 30 days?

**Offline Store (training):** The churn-prediction and expansion-propensity models both pull point-in-time snapshots of these five features for 50,000 accounts. Because both models read the same Feature Store, they are guaranteed to use identical definitions — no silent divergence.

**Online Store (inference):** When the Account Expansion agent evaluates an account in a Salesforce Agentforce or Microsoft Copilot workflow, it calls the Feature Store's online API to retrieve the latest values for that DUNS number in <15ms. The agent combines them with the model's weights to produce an 'expand now' recommendation with a SHAP-style explanation: 'Paydex improved 12 points, headcount grew 23% YoY, and intent signals spiked — expansion probability 81%.'

**Governance payoff:** When a customer asks 'Why did your AI flag us for upsell?', D&B can point to the Feature Store registry, show the exact feature values at the moment of scoring, their source lineage back to raw trade data, and the timestamp of computation. That is the Explainability First / Ground Truth principle made operationally real — not a slide-deck claim but a queryable audit log.
